narration: Welcome to the Manuscripts gallery. This is a 17th‑century Mughal Quran, bound to 30 by 20 centimeters, written in fine naskh calligraphy on paper and illuminated with gold‑leaf floral borders and geometric frames that echo the court ateliers of the time. The manuscript reflects the same lavish gold‑leaf technique used in imperial Persian and Mughal secular works, a testament to the emperors’ patronage of religious art. It is part of our “The Holy Quran” exhibition and was acquired by the National Museum for the Government of India’s Manuscripts collection. Enjoy the intricate beauty and the quiet reverence of this treasured page.
